newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nintendo rises on plan to cut game price.
newsitem.headline: Nintendo rises on plan to cut game price.

text.p: Shares of Nintendo Co Ltd jumped on Thursday morning, cheered by a newspaper report that the firm plans to cut the U.S. price of its 64-bit video game machine "Nintendo 64" to about $150 from $199 currently, traders said.
By 0210 GMT, the share price had risen 150 yen to 8,570. Turnover was 193,200 shares.

The Mainichi Shimbun said on Thursday that the move was aimed to counter rival Sony Corp, which announced earlier this week that it had cut the U.S. price of its unit Sony Computer Entertainment Inc's 32-bit Playstation by 25 percent to $149.
A Nintendo official told Reuters on Thursday that its U.S. unit was responsible for Nintendo's game machine business in the United States and he could not comment on prices.
